description:
Three citations that will not survive their document's relocation are repointed to a form that resolves from the archive, before the containers holding those documents are archived.

## Background

An artifact outside the development root is retained where it is: the archive schedules no destination for it and leaves its source untouched. A document that cites such an artifact through a relative or root-relative reference, and that is itself relocated into the archive, therefore carries a citation that resolves to nothing once the move happens. The execution-time layout validator exempts these edges rather than refusing the plan, because demanding that a retained target stay reachable would forbid relocating anything that cites one.

Most occurrences are harmless. Where the citing document is copied rather than relocated, its live original stays in place and keeps resolving, and only the frozen archive snapshot carries a dead link — which is what an archived snapshot of a moved-on repository is. The exceptions are the citing documents that relocate: those leave their source path entirely, so the archived copy is the only copy and the citation is dead everywhere.

Two such documents exist, carrying three citations between them:

- `dev/active/gate-examples.md` cites `/docs/tutorials/first-workflow.md`, a root-relative reference.
- `dev/active/2b9a80fb-audit-notes.md` cites `../../mcp-server/README.md` and `../../mcp-server/curated-tools.json`.

The measurement that found them reads each container's plan and reports every edge whose target is retained outside the development root and whose citing artifact has a destination; the three above are the subset whose citing artifact relocates.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each of the three citations resolves to its intended target when read from the citing document's archived location.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each of the three citations resolves to its intended target when read from the citing document's current location, for as long as it remains there.
- [hard] REQ-03: No plan over the affected containers reports an edge whose target is retained outside the development root and whose citing artifact is scheduled for relocation.
- [hard] REQ-04: Whole-repository validation passes, with every document reference resolving.

## Notes

REQ-01 and REQ-02 together rule out simply deleting the citations, and rule out a form that trades one location's correctness for the other's.

The citing documents are historical records. Their prose is not rewritten beyond the citation form itself.

Per `@/issue/8e071e18/decision/D-14`.
title: Repoint citations that do not survive their document's relocation
